cohort: 34 pregnant women with SARS-CoV-2 infection and preterm birth compared with a control group of 48 healthy women with preterm birth
finding: Pregnant women with SARS-CoV-2 infection and preterm birth had a higher rate of cesarean delivery and were more likely to experience severe respiratory symptoms, decreased oxygen saturation, increased inflammatory markers, severe pulmonary lesions, and decreased lymphocytes compared to healthy women with preterm birth.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery was 82% in the study group (pregnant women with SARS-CoV-2 infection and preterm birth) versus 6% for the control group (healthy women with preterm birth).
